analysis.title: Macro Roadmap: Can Christmas Come Early?
key_insights: GS sees conditions for equities to squeeze higher into year end: a large equity sell-off, lower multiples, much lighter positioning and supportive seasonals.
Deleveraging in the AI complex was extreme. Net/gross de-risking in GS's US prime book is one of the most aggressive episodes of the past decade, and Thursday's Nasdaq sell-off was a ~5 sigma move.

MSCI P/Es have derated to 35-year historical averages. GS is less concerned about supply constraints on the AI build-out (capital, permitting, energy) than about demand or monetization risk, which quarterly earnings will test.
Little incremental information on AI demand is expected before Q4 earnings. A Middle East re-escalation is the named headwind to the equity view.
Equities absorbed a stronger CPI print, hawkish Fed comments, a rate sell-off, an oil rally and Nvidia news flow this week, which GS reads as supportive market structure.

US CPI surprised to the upside in both September and October, with broad-based beats. Producer and import prices have accelerated, and global import price inflation for manufactured goods is above pandemic-era rates.

Price pressure has spread beyond energy and AI-related products to chemicals, plastics and paper. Upstream increases take 6-12 months to pass through, so Q1 is the test (January effect, price resets, wage negotiations).
Companies have absorbed much of the input cost increase in margins. If demand cannot absorb pass-through, the labour market may take the strain.

The Fed turned more hawkish this week while the ECB and BoE point to gradualism, conditional on no broad pass-through or wage strength. Central banks had shifted dovish in October in response to the equity wobble and credit pressure.
GS finds near-term rate direction tricky after yields re-priced higher this week, but sees a risk of higher inflation surprises through Q1 and recommends being long front-end inflation.

The long end of the European curve looks rich: long forwards such as 20y10y are the only G4 points richer since the Iran crisis began in February. EUR 10s30s at -13bp looks too flat versus GS's fair value model.

Steepeners were the epicentre of September's European deleveraging, so positioning is extremely light. This year's Dutch pension reform set-up differs from last year's and could have a larger market impact. Risks to steepeners are energy and Q1 price resets, so GS suggests a front-end beta hedge, a pairing with front-end inflation longs, or being short the forwards.

BoE hiked in November and guided the market toward one more hike, with timing between December and February unclear. It wants to avoid guiding to more than two total hikes this cycle (including Pill) without explicit second-round effects.
BoE inflation projections peak at 4.9% in Q2 next year but the November tone was less hawkish than that implies. GS argues the high baseline skews risks dovishly.
The market prices nearly 20bps for December and 39bps cumulatively through February. GS likes receiving these two meetings and holding UK rate longs strictly at the very front end.

GS's summary: 2026 has been a poor year for macro and fading consensus trades has worked. GS expects an equity squeeze into December, European long-end shorts are under-owned ahead of Dutch reform in January, and a strong January inflation effect would make duration harder.
earnings_insights: Q4 earnings are the next incremental information on AI capex monetization. GS says their weight and scrutiny will increase next year.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity sell-off, lower multiples, light positioning, supportive seasonals and MSCI P/Es at 35-year averages set up a squeeze higher into year end.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex monetization is uncertain, inflation pressure persists with a hawkish Fed, and the Middle East could re-escalate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Middle East re-escalation, or evidence that AI demand or monetization is at risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Companies absorb input costs in margins and the ECB and BoE stay gradual.
tension_points.bear_case: Upstream producer and import price increases pass through to consumers in Q1 via the January effect and price and wage resets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q1 price resets and wage negotiations fail to add upward pressure.
